content:
As WhatsApp moves closer to the official rollout of its username feature, the messaging app now allows users to save a contact's username, name and phone number together. Here are the details.

A username field is being added when saving contacts, rolling out first to some WhatsApp users.

While username-based identification has long been standard on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently begun moving away from relying solely on phone numbers to identify users.

WhatsApp began rolling out username reservations earlier this year, giving users the chance to secure their preferred usernames before the feature officially launched, to prevent impersonation by scammers.

Then, just a few weeks ago, WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is adding a username field when users save a new contact. The username field appears between the name field and the phone number field.

WABetaInfo reports:

WABetaInfo says that the username field appears to be rolling out to some users on both the Beta and stable versions of WhatsApp.

When testing on the latest stable version, although the field is displayed, entering an existing username still returns the message "This username is not on WhatsApp".

That said, this is undoubtedly another step forward for WhatsApp in catching up with industry standards, filling in a basic feature that many have long felt should have been there from the start.
